This report describes a lab which uses the STM32L432KC MCU  timers to play music given a matrix structure of notes and the number of milliseconds that the notes are played for. This lab took me about 24 hours to complete.    

### Hardware Specifications
The setup can play a set of musical notes with rests at the correct pitches and for the correct amount of time. It utilizes the 3362P 10K potentiomter to control the volume of the speaker that outputs the music and an LM386 audio amplifier to limit the amount of current that the speaker pulls from the MCU. 

### Software and Microcontroller Design
This lab uses two timers, timer 6 and timer 7 with custom header files to access all of the registers from memory using structures. An example of the structured register access is included below. All other code can be found in my [lab 4 GitHub repository](https://github.com/klatvakoski/katie_speaker_lab4).

### Timer functionality 
#### Timer 6
Timer 6 was used to produce a wave at a specific frequency. This wave was output directly to pin, PB6, which then input that signal into the LM386 audio amplifier, and subsequently the speaker. Timer 6 is driven by the MSI oscillator at 4 MHz, and configured using the PSC prescaler to drive it at 1 MHz. A max-count value is determined for each desired frequency using the following equation:
$$
"Max count" = \frac{1 MHz}{f_des}
$$


### AI Prototype

My reflection on the outcome of this might be fairly standard. The output was better when given the extra file and info. Therefore, when coding using an LLM, it might be helpful to give it as much information as possible, so that it can work within your constraints better. I think the one downside of this is that it doesn't allow the LLM as much ingenuity. For example, if you specified a constraint of using combinational logic in a certain case, but the LLM actually has seen a use-case of something else that implements your desired design better, then you would probably want to see that.
